New section 482 of the Bhartiya Nagrik Surksha Sanhita, 2023 for grant of anticipatory bail, as he is under apprehension of his arrest, in connection with FIR No.104/2024, registered at Police Station Pandhurna District Chhindwara 2 MCRC-26913-2024 (MP) for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 120-B, 409 of the IPC and Section 6(1) of the Madhya Pradesh Nikshepako Ke Hito Ka Sanrakshan Adhiniyam, 2000.

sentences.text: 3. As per prosecution story, one Preeti made a complaint at Police Station Pandurna against the applicants.
Nephew of complainant Gyandeep was working in Matra Seva India Nidhi Limited and he informed the complainant that said Company is given better interest on FD of Rs.1,00,000/-.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Complainant invested Rs.3,50,000/- in the Company on promise of better interest.

After maturity,
when she went to office, she found that Directors of the Company have closed the office and have cheated the complainant.
4. Learned counsel appearing for applicants submitted that applicants are innocent and have falsely been implicated in the case.
Investigation is complete and charge sheet has been filed.
First application of applicant Keshav was dismissed for want of prosecution.
Applicant is only worker in the office.
He did not receive any amount nor any receipt of depositing of money.
No case is made out against the applicant.
He has not cheated the complainant and no specific role has been attributed to him.
Co-accused persons have already been granted bail by this court and on the ground of parity, applicant Keshav deserves to be released on anticipatory bail.
5. Learned counsel appearing for applicant Shailesh Bilgaiya submitted that applicant is only a worker in the said company.
He has not cheated the complainant.
His case is on parity with other co-accused persons, who was released on bail.
He is suffering from kidney disease and is under treatment from jail.
Applicant is permanent resident of Nagpur.
In these circumstances, applicant may be granted bail.

6. Learned Dy. Government Advocate appearing for the State opposed the 3 MCRC-26913-2024 bail applications and submitted that applicants are main accused in the case and they are Directors of the company.
Hence, they may not be granted bail.
7. On going through the report produced by Town Inspector, it is found that 11 Investors had invested an amount of Rs.17,07,225/- in the said company.
Documents in respect of said investment was seized from the company.
Offences are serious in nature.
Applicants have misrepresented before the Court.
They were not the workers of the company, whereas they are Directors of the Company.
Another co-accused namely Preeti who was granted bail was cashier.
Now, it has come to light that as many as there are 11 Investors in the case who had been cheated and offence under section 409 of the IPC is punishable upto life imprisonment.
Case of applicants is not on parity with other co-accused person.
Preeti was cashier and Manager in the Company and not a Director.
Ganesh Pachori has filed an application for regular bail.
Applicant Keshav has filed application under section 438 of the Cr.P.C. and he is absconding from law.
He is required for further investigation.
In these circumstances, bail application filed by applicant Shailesh Bilgaiya is dismissed.
Similarly application under section 438 of the Cr.P.C. filed by applicant Keshav is also dismissed.
